headline.text: Kymenlaakso's crude curative treatment share is 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

details.text: In curative shares digitised from Kuva 16 (precision ±0.5 percentage points), the gap holds after age adjustment for men at 17.9% (95% CI 13.9–22.9) versus 26.7% nationally (the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value), while for women at 22.6% (95% CI 16.8–29.3) versus 26.9% the 95% confidence interval includes it.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can receive several types, Kymenlaakso has higher crude shares of life-prolonging treatment at 37.6% (95% CI 33.8–41.5; n=222/591) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally and symptomatic treatment at 51.3% (95% CI 47.2–55.3; n=303/591) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally, with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

A multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting is recorded for a crude share of 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) of Kymenlaakso patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO MDT codes capture only direct patient contacts and measure recording practice rather than care.

headline.text: Relatively complete treatment recording is a reasonable inference in Kymenlaakso, but crude county shares lack stage adjustment and public registry data do not measure pathway waiting times.

details.text: Kymenlaakso's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6; n=97/591) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally; its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value (entirely below it), an inference consistent with relatively complete treatment recording that makes a low curative share less likely to be only a recording artefact.

The county table's treatment shares are crude and have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted (county-level age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex), and separately they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types (concerning diagnosis concordance only, not treatment or MDT recording), whereas public data do not measure symptom onset, referral dates, or specialist visit and treatment start dates, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, and occupational health is not mentioned.

Preliminary, unpublished national figures—which are national averages, not county-specific—report an average of 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland (56 days patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, the longest stage), alongside 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark.

headline.text: To address Kymenlaakso's low crude curative share and MDT recording gaps, the team recommends tracking access times, standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination, and publishing recording completeness.

details.text: The team recommends reporting access times (referral to specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start) using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (for 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers; the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for cancer suspicion, while the STM roadmap (measure 3.1.2) plans national pathway descriptions and cancer-specific access times for five cancers by 2026–2028.

The team recommends a KYS-modelled referral template, pulmonologist referral when symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, and a named diagnostic-phase contact; referrals currently follow local instructions, mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower specialist urgency ratings, and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation (primary-care referral criteria and recommended time limits) is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding to read gaps as data-quality signals; lung cancer data reporting is incomplete and Finland has no cancer quality registry, while the STM roadmap (measure 3.2.1) plans a national quality registry with a 90% data-coverage indicator including stage.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact
